toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are tied to Kestrel, not to pay or the firm-wide hours increase. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. Other groups' attrition is normal, which argues against general market mobility. The hours target applied to every group, so it doesn't explain one group's spike. Pay is also not the driver. Group salaries sit at the same market band as the rest of the firm. Brennick & Stowe is £3–5k higher, not £15k. Most leavers took equal or lower pay. A £12k retention payment would cost £228k and probably wouldn't fix the problem. I'd advise against it, and against closing the review.

What we can't yet separate is Kestrel's workload from Dorian Faulk's supervision. All Kestrel associates report to him and he supervises on nothing else, so the two overlap completely. The survey points to both: weekend work and humiliating late-night corrections. Moving supervision or paying £160k for contract reviewers would each be a guess now.

Next step: commission the roughly £9k confidential external interviews, structured to separate workload from supervision. Four leavers have already agreed to take part. Meanwhile, add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Confidence is high on pay and hours, moderate on Kestrel.
